* — `Summary.Observe` skips records with `Valid == false` before folding them into per-metric counts and totals. This is the path used by `Aggregate`, which powers `--summary`, so invalid records no longer inflate `count=` or `total=` lines.

**`internal/report/aggregate.go`** — `Distinct` (the CLI's `--names-only` answer) applies the same rule, so an invalid record's name can't inflate the distinct-name count either.

## Why this approach

The pipeline's `filter` stage (`DropInvalid`) is opt-in, so reporting can't rely on batches arriving pre-filtered — the report package itself is now the guarantee that invalid records are excluded regardless of pipeline configuration. The two report entry points that answer questions about a set of batches (`Aggregate`/`Summary` and `Distinct`) both skip `Valid == false` records; the existing test's convention of setting `Valid: true` explicitly on well-formed records confirms the zero value means invalid.

No existing tests were changed. `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` pass (verified with the full suite, plus a throwaway test confirming invalid records are excluded from both summary lines and distinct-name counting, which I then removed).
